candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And after that I saw all the secrets of the heavens, and how the kingdom is divided, and how the actions of men are weighed in the balance' — the cosmic-balance image. Tewahedo eschatology of judgment as actual weighing (with Michael often depicted as the angel of the scales in church iconography) draws on this verse as scriptural anchor, paralleling Dan 5:27 and standing in lineage with the Egyptian Maat-tradition that Ethiopian iconography preserves through a Christianised filter.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'For the Lord has separated the day and the night, and the spirits of light and darkness, and apportioned them their seasons' — apportioning theology. Tewahedo wisdom tradition reads this verse in tandem with Gen 1:4-5 as the textual basis for the doctrine that even darkness is ordered toward divine purpose, not autonomous evil — a key node in the Tewahedo theodicy framework.
